articles.title: Your first load
articles.summary: Shovel, wheelbarrow, pickup and your first sale.
steps: Walk onto your field with {forward}, {back}, {left} and {right}. Aim down at the grass and click the left mouse button to dig. The shovel must be emptied before another bite.
Aim into the wheelbarrow and click to empty the shovel. Use {interact} at its handles to take it. Push to the pickup's tailgate and press {tip} to transfer the load.
You can also park the pickup beside your dig and shovel straight into its bed. Keep topsoil separate: it pays well, and clay mixed into it reduces its grade.
articles.trouble: An empty shovel click digs; a loaded shovel click tips. If the barrow will not transfer, get its front close to the pickup's tailgate and check that the pickup has room.

articles.title: Weigh, grade and sell
articles.summary: Turn actual cargo into income at Ashby Aggregates.
steps: Get into your loaded road vehicle with {interact}. Open the map with {map}; Ashby Aggregates is reached along Mill Lane, through Ashby and onto Quarry Road.
Stop on the depot weighbridge and wait for a ticket. Drive to the matching material bay, put the tailgate inside the bay and press {tip}.

A clean load in the correct bay earns the best grade. Check Depot prices before hauling. Mixed cargo can be sold in the mixed-fill bay, but pays less. Material still in a bucket or stockpile has not been sold.
articles.trouble: If unloading asks you to weigh in, stop on the scale again. Changing the cargo after weighing invalidates the ticket. A little material may remain when a buyer or vehicle limit is reached.

articles.title: Choose and look after machines
articles.summary: Buy or rent the capacity and reach your site needs.
steps: Open Ashby Plant with {shop}. Compare model size, reach, bucket volume, breakout force and price. A small rental lets you try controls before buying; return rentals empty and on time.
The cheapest compact digger is a useful first step from the shovel. Pair its output with enough haulage capacity, and park the loading vehicle within the arm's reach.

Use Fleet to select and locate machines, fit upgrades, arrange service or sell equipment you have outgrown. {repair} near a machine requests service or repair; a mobile mechanic can attend a stranded vehicle.
articles.trouble: A low bank balance can stop a job before it starts. Keep money for diesel, repairs and wages. A broken machine needs repair; selecting a different control mode will not fix it.

articles.title: Dig, swing and load
articles.summary: Assisted controls, Direct controls and the right attachment.
steps: Get into a digger with {interact}. In Assisted control, aim the bucket at your field and hold the left mouse button. Swing over a nearby bed or stockpile bay and click to dump.

{controls} switches between Assisted and Direct controls. In Direct, use {boomUp}/{boomDown} for the boom, {stickOut}/{stickIn} for the stick, {bucketCurl}/{bucketDump} for the bucket and {slewLeft}/{slewRight} to swing. {jump} switches between tracking and arm control.

Use {attachments} to choose an attachment. Empty the bucket and finish its movement first. Teeth must move into the ground to cut; a loaded bucket may still have spare volume. Press {survey} to inspect what you are digging.
articles.trouble: A normal bucket cannot cut intact bedrock. Fit a compatible breaker to leave rubble for the bucket, or prepare a contractor cut. Rocks that have already been loosened can be loaded normally.

articles.title: Haulage and trailers
articles.summary: Hitch, weigh and unload without overloading the combination.
steps: A tractor and tipping trailer are separate purchases. Stop the tractor close to the trailer and hitch them in Fleet. The trailer's own weight counts against the tractor's gross towing limit.
Drive with {forward}, {back}, {left} and {right}. Brake before reversing and use {jump} for the handbrake. {precision} gives a lighter pedal; {cruise} holds road speed when available.
Load the trailer, weigh the complete combination and put the trailer's tailgate over the delivery bay before pressing {tip}. Keep loads low and take slopes and bends slowly.
articles.trouble: If a trailer refuses more material, check both its own capacity and the tractor's gross towing limit. Detach only while stopped and clear of other vehicles.

articles.title: Read the field
articles.summary: Separate useful layers and plan access before digging deeper.
steps: Press {survey} and aim at the ground to see its current layers and the depth to bedrock. Deposited heaps and compacted fill are included; this is today's ground, not an untouched reserve map.

In Quarry operations → Work areas, choose a field, area and target material. Compare the nine boreholes and their layer profiles; least cover suggests the shallowest sampled layer with at least 80% target by volume. Save a face plan to mark that exact point.
Strip and store topsoil separately, then work clay, sand and gravel in clean passes. Leave space for a ramp, loading pad and a turning area. Loose slopes can settle and undercut walls can collapse.
articles.trouble: Refresh boreholes after digging to compare cover and layer thickness with your saved plan. Plans survive navigation changes and reload. Work-area figures are sampled estimates; actual cargo mass determines sale purity, and the ground between samples can differ.

articles.title: Build ramps, roads and pads
articles.summary: Use real cut and spoil to make your site driveable.
steps: On foot, press {works} to open the planner. Choose a haul road, ramp or level area. Mark its start and end, inspect the preview, then confirm the build.
The planner uses material from the cut and loose heaps within reach. Roads and ramps also need gravel for their surface; level pads need no gravel surfacing. Spare material is left beside the works.
Lengthen a steep ramp, bring suitable spoil close enough and move parked vehicles out of the footprint. Nothing is spent until a valid build is confirmed.
articles.trouble: Right-click cancels the preview. If a fill or surfacing quote is short, tip the requested material nearby. A level pad is often the simplest first earthwork.

articles.title: Store and process material
articles.summary: Bays, crushing, screening and finite production queues.
steps: Buy stockpile bays in the plant dealer. Tip real cargo into a bay, or dump a digger bucket into it. Keep feed, clean products and unwanted material separate.

A crusher turns broken rock into a gravel/sand blend. A screener separates the selected material and leaves rejects in the feed bay. In Production, choose the recipe, bays and batch size, then review the cost and reserved space.

Queue a finite number of batches if you want the plant to keep working. A queue waits for feed, space, maintenance and your cash reserve. Upgrade bay walls for more storage and service worn plants in Plant workshop.
articles.trouble: Leave output room and cancellation room. Cancelled batches return held feed, retain the paid operating cost and pause future orders. Finished product still needs loading, weighing and hauling.

articles.title: Open bedrock with a contractor cut
articles.summary: Survey, drill, charge, clear the field and load the rubble.
steps: Choose Rock blasting in Quarry operations. Strip the whole footprint to bedrock and clear old rubble. Pick a point on the field map, or use the point you are surveying.
Book drilling, then book the charging crew when drilling finishes. Preparation takes game time and each stage has its own cost. Keep the drilled ground unchanged.

Move yourself, vehicles, trailers and the barrow outside the marked boundary. Start the countdown; {interact} stops it from the field. Intrusion also stops it until you give another firing command. Load the loosened rock with an ordinary bucket.
articles.trouble: A cut does not create inventory or make a sale. Clear the rubble before drilling deeper; the rock reserve is finite. Cancelling keeps the crew costs already paid.

articles.title: Supply regional buyers
articles.summary: Nursery, concrete yard and roadworks demand.
steps: Regional trade shows each buyer's accepted products, purity requirements, prices and remaining daily demand. Choose a destination to guide your delivery.
Stop on that buyer's scale, then move the tailgate over its delivery pad and press {tip}. Only accepted material up to the remaining demand is sold; the rest stays in your vehicle.
Regular deliveries build supplier relationships and improve prices. Quotas reset with the business day. Customer jobs on the Jobs board remain optional.
articles.trouble: A home/depot ticket still needs the correct load, and changed cargo must be weighed again. Compare today's buyer quote with depot prices before committing to the trip.

articles.title: Build a working crew
articles.summary: Operators, drivers, maintenance and the office.
steps: Hire staff when a post becomes available. Assign an operator to a digger and position the loading vehicle within reach. Assign a driver and choose the material and destination for the haul.
Workers use the same real material and machinery as you. Give them usable access and enough loading/receiving room. Reassign a worker before taking over their machine yourself.
Wages are paid each morning. Experienced workers improve through completed work. An office worker can handle optional customer orders, but clean independent sales remain a valid way to grow.
articles.trouble: If a job waits, check the loading position, feed material, vehicle condition, destination demand and cash. Waiting does not create a free load.

articles.title: Keep the company solvent
articles.summary: Running costs, investment, loans and recovery from a bad day.
steps: The Bank statement separates purchases and ordinary running costs. Daily reports show income, costs, excavation, sales and processing. Sale income is earned only when material is delivered.

Keep cash for fuel, wages, servicing and queued production. Selling a spare machine or a clean stockpile load can release cash. The bank offers loans against the business, with payments due each morning.
Service useful machines before they break, return rentals on time and pause production orders you cannot support. Debt is recoverable; focus on a manageable clean load instead of buying more kit.
articles.trouble: Turning off the step-by-step guide does not change prices, rewards or difficulty. Milestones and customer jobs are optional directions, not a requirement to keep working.

articles.title: Save, back up and continue
articles.summary: Manual slots, autosaves, recovery copies and portable files.
steps: Open the pause menu with Esc and choose Save Game. Manual slots keep one previous revision for recovery. Autosaves also run periodically during active play when enabled in Settings.
Open Load Game to see slot summaries and recovery copies. Export downloads a portable save file; Import checks a file and lets you choose a manual slot before storing it.
Save and quit to the main menu when ending a session. Keep exported files somewhere you control: browser storage belongs to this browser and can be cleared by its settings.
articles.trouble: A failed save leaves the existing copy available. A damaged main copy can recover from the previous revision. If browser storage is full, export your current company before clearing anything.

articles.title: Expand into neighbouring fields
articles.summary: Buy room to grow and choose geology that suits your equipment.
steps: Open Land in Quarry operations. South Meadow has deeper sand; East Ridge has shallow rock. Survey ground gives sampled cover and reserve estimates before you commit to the purchase.

Buy the field outright when you have enough cash. Guide to entrance marks its access opening. Your site machines can cross the marked connection from the existing field or yard; haulage and your home processing plants serve every property.

Choose a new working face in Work areas. Separate its layers, plan a loading pad and ramp, then haul real material back to the yard or a buyer. Rock blasting has a Field selector so cuts use the correct reserve.
articles.trouble: A field for sale can be inspected but cannot be dug, tipped on or used for earthworks. Buying it preserves existing holes, piles and cargo everywhere else. Access strips connect the properties; excavations stay within the actual field boundaries.
